title: Negotiated Tranches for Top Accounts — Fractional Delivery Playbook
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description: Problem: Strategic customers escalate commercial asks that exceed standard roadmap capacity. Single-monolithic commitments force either long delays or full scope overcommitment. Proposal: introduce a negotiated tranche mechanism where commitments to top accounts are split into small, time-boxed 'tranches' (e.g., 20-40% scope slices) with objectively measurable verification gates before next tranche is unlocked. This reduces risk, makes partial deliveries predictable, and gives legal/sales a clear signal for entitlement credits. The playbook defines negotiation templates, verification gates (SLOs, acceptance tests, usage signals), rollback criteria, and credit mechanics.
background: Current intake practice uses binary accept/decline with ad-hoc carve-outs. Several revenue-impact cases in 2025 showed missed expectations when scope drifted. This ticket consolidates learnings from ACME PoC (incident summary linked below) and creates a repeatable tranche workflow for future enterprise negotiations.
goals: Reduce committed scope surprise for Eng by 50% for top-account features in pilot cohort
Provide Sales & Legal standardized tranche terms to shorten contract negotiation time by 30%
Enable measurable roll-forward or roll-back decisions per tranche using objective gates
Ship first pilot tranche for 3 accounts in Q2 with telemetry-based verification
acceptance_criteria: Tranche contract template reviewed and signed off by Legal
Console UI wireframe for tranche status visible to account teams (QA + Product) exists
Engineering has implementation plan with capacity estimate per tranche and rollback playbook
Pilot agreements signed with at least 2 strategic accounts and kickoffs scheduled
Dashboard widgets show tranche progress: feature completion, SLO attainment, activation metrics
tasks: Draft tranche contract template and credit model (PM + Legal)
Define verification gates: functional test suite, latency SLO target, adoption threshold
Create Console mockups for tranche status and customer-facing progress notices (Design)
Engineering: estimate effort per tranche and identify non-negotiable dependencies
Sales/Success: identify pilot accounts and finalize pilot SLAs
Build dashboards and alerts for gate signals (Observability)
Run pilot with three accounts, collect feedback and iterate
decisions: Use tranche size range 20-40% (configurable per account) to balance value delivery and predictability
Verification gates must include at least one product metric (activation or usage), one reliability metric (p95 latency < target), and a customer acceptance step
Credits for unmet gates are issued as 'priority credits' usable against future roadmap slots rather than cash refunds
risks: Accounts may attempt to game verification gates to expedite future tranches
Engineering throughput misestimation could lead to tranche slippage and customer dissatisfaction
Legal complexity around conditional delivery may slow contract execution
Instrumentation gaps could make verification noisy or delayed
mitigations: Include objective, telemetry-backed gates and require a short acceptance window from the customer
Enforce conservative capacity buffer in initial tranches and require dependency sign-off
Early Legal review and a small clause bank for tranche language to reuse across customers
Observability sprint to create minimal viable telemetry for tranche gates before pilot start
pilot_plan: Select 3 pilot accounts: ACME Corp, BrightBank, NovaAI (mutual NDAs in place)
Run 12-week pilot per account with up to 3 tranches each
Week 0: sign tranche agreement and baseline metrics; Week 4: deliver tranche 1; Week 8: evaluate gates; Week 12: unlock tranche 2 or issue credits
Collect qualitative feedback from account champions at each tranche gate
